correctness.rationale: For any finite identity frame, trace additivity gives an exact localization-energy sum equal to \(\tau(1_B)\), while positivity forces each frame vector to have module norm at most one. This proves the lower operator-norm bound. The upper bound follows from \(0\le\langle z,z\rangle_B\le\|z\|^2 1_B\). For \(M_{r,s}\), localization is scaled Hilbert--Schmidt norm, whose exact ratio to operator norm is \(\sqrt{\min\{r,s\}}\); the minimum frame count is exactly \(\lceil s/r\rceil\) by rank subadditivity and a block partial-isometry construction. All quantifiers, boundary regimes, trace scaling, and equality witnesses were checked analytically.

value.rationale: The localization map is the central Banach-to-Hilbert bridge in the recent Gelfand-triple framework, while finite module frames encode finite projectivity/generator complexity. The theorem supplies a dimension-sensitive quantitative bridge between these two structures: large trace mass and small localization distortion force many module generators. The exact rectangular matrix classification shows that the ceiling obstruction is not merely qualitative or a loose estimate: it recovers the true minimal frame length for every pair of matrix sizes and every positive trace scaling. This gives a natural calibrated invariant rather than an arbitrary slice or a numerical recomputation.
